Definition: from εἵλη (the sun's ray) and G2919; judged by sunlight, i.e. tested as genuine (figuratively):--pure, sincere.
BiblicalUsage: This word means sincere or pure, tested by sunlight, and it occurs twice. Paul prays that the Philippians may approve the excellent things and be sincere and without offence until the day of Christ, and Peter says he writes to stir up their pure minds by way of remembrance. The picture is the same: a life with nothing hidden from the light.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God wants a pure mind, not just pure actions, because what I think in the dark shapes what I do in the light.
